messages:
Ravi Shah: Heads-up — Aurora (fintech) wants a week-long POC to move inference from their current vendor to Redwood. CTO listed three blockers: API/response parity, surge billing during live demo, and an enterprise security questionnaire. Can eng/security/sales triage?
Tara Nguyen: I'll coordinate the parity checks. Do they expect streaming events + candidate lists for reranking?
Ravi Shah: Yes streaming chat and `candidates[]` with scores. They also rely on stable `message_id` for threading.
Miles Carter: Typical parity issues: event names, role labels, usage fields (prompt/completion split), and streaming chunk format. We'll need a thin compatibility proxy that both accepts their payloads and emits their expected response shape.
Aisha Rahman: Security received their vendor pack (50 Qs). Immediate asks: SOC2 + ISO cert dates, KMS/CMK support, SSO (SAML/OIDC), subprocessor list, and ability to enforce data residency in EU. Also a request for a signed DPA and subprocessors appendix.
LegalBot: [auto] Questionnaire link uploaded: https://redwood-internal/sec/aurora-poc-2026
Tara Nguyen: Example of their current call: curl POST https://api.aurora.ai/v1/chat -H 'Authorization: Bearer AURORA-KEY' -d '{"model":"aurora-chat-xl","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Analyze Q3 revenue"}],"stream":true}'
Tara Nguyen: Redwood equivalent would be POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat.stream with body model->redwood alias and messages->input. Proxy should translate and preserve `message_id` and `candidate_id`.
Miles Carter: For streaming we'll map their `event: chunk` / `event: final` to Redwood's chunk types and ensure partials include the same `delta` shape. We should also populate `usage.prompt_tokens` and `usage.completion_tokens` in final responses so their billing hooks keep working.
Aisha Rahman: On KMS: Aurora wants customer-managed keys. For Private we support CMKs directly (AWS/GCP). For hosted we can offer envelope encryption with customer KMS inside VPC private deployment or a limited BYOK pilot; I'll put that text in the questionnaire.
Ravi Shah: Procurement question: "If traffic spikes 1.5-2x during the demo, will we throttle or bill overage?"
Miles Carter: For POC we usually offer trial credits + temporary burst allowance with explicit caps. Suggest soft alerts at 1.1x and a hard cap at 3x; finance needs to OK overage pricing.
Tara Nguyen: Reranker flow note: they POST /v1/rerank with `candidate_ids` returned earlier. Proxy must ensure candidate ids are stable or provide a mapping service that resolves their ids to Redwood outputs. I'll include deterministic id generation (hash-based) in the proxy plan.
Aisha Rahman: They also asked for maintenance window policy and an SLA of 99.95. We can offer Dedicated + SLA addendum; Legal to draft APL.
LegalBot: [auto] DPA and subprocessor appendix templates available: https://redwood-internal/legal/dpa-templates
Ravi Shah: Timeline: exec demo in 6 business days. Can we commit to a minimal parity run (8 canonical prompts + 2 rerank flows) and a completed security questionnaire draft by EOD +3?
Tara Nguyen: I'll assemble the canonical prompt set (include code, HTML, few-shot, and adversarial inputs). ETA EOD +1.
Miles Carter: I'll spin up a staging proxy and run side-by-side checks. ETA EOD +2.
Aisha Rahman: Draft security answers + KMS wording + SOC2/ISO artifacts to procurement by EOD +3.
Ravi Shah: Action items: Tara prompt set (EOD+1), Miles staging proxy & parity tests (EOD+2), Aisha security draft & attachments (EOD+3), Ravi to confirm demo invite and run kickoff tomorrow 9am PT.
Tara Nguyen: I'll join kickoff.
Miles Carter: Same.
Aisha Rahman: I'll be there for security Qs.
Ravi Shah: Great. Keep updates short in this thread — post brief check-ins only. :rocket:
